newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Euro hedgers seen long-term SAfrica bond investors.
newsitem.headline: Euro hedgers seen long-term SAfrica bond investors.

text.p: Foreigners who have been heavy buyers of local rand bonds as a hedge against Eurorand issues this year are likely to prove relatively long-term investors in South Africa, the Reserve Bank said on Thursday.

The central bank noted in its latest Quarterly Bulletin that portfolio investment flows were traditionally highly volatile and could therefore have a destabilising effect on the general macroeconomic equilibirum.
But it took comfort from the fact that a significant portion of non-resident purchases of South African bonds this year formed a hedge against Eurorand issues.

"To the extent that these investment were the hedging counterpart of some of the Eurorand bond issues which had been made in the first quarter, they represented a relatively longer-term investment in the economy," the bank said.

"Indeed, some of the Eurobond issues of 7.1 billion rand issued in the first quarter of 1997 were hedged in the South African market through the purchase of bonds with a maturity of between one and five years."

Another important consequence of the Eurorand bond issues was that they triggered increased forward purchases of rand, or forward sales of dollars, thereby contributing to a more balanced position in the domestic forward forex market, the bank noted.
Net inflows of capital not related to reserves in the first quarter of 1997 rose to 3.6 billion rand from 3.3 billion the last quarter of 1996.
Long-term capital movements changed from an outflow of 1.2 billion in the fourth quarter of 1996 to an inflow of 4.8 billion.
By far the greatest part of the inflow of long-term capital reflected foreign purchases of bonds and shares.

The net payment for purchases of bonds by non-residents amounted to 3.9 billion in the first quarter, and a further 2.2 billion of net purchases were left unsettled at the end of the period. Foreign net purchases of shares in the first quarter amounted to 3.5 billion rand.

Short-term capital movements changed to an outflow of 1.2 billion rand in the first quarter from an inflow of 4.5 billion in the fourth quarter of last year, mainly due to the repayment of loans by the private banking sector.

The central bank noted that the large-scale interest shown by non-residents in South African securities in the firt quarter had contributed to an increase in average daily turnover on the foreign exchange market to $6.7 billion.

At the same time, the rand's appreciation against the dollar had contributed to a slowdown in the expansion of activity in the forward foreign exchange market and an improvement in the balance between sales and purchases in the forward foreign exchange market.
"It also resulted in substantial surpluses accruing to the Reserve Bank on account of transactions in the forward foreign exchange market," it said.
